title: Simple, premium, doodle-first
question: The visual world is now fixed. Which mobile composition gets the balance right?

options.label: Doodle Scene
options.lineage: one authored Anchor doodle followed by a quiet native schedule
options.body: The original focus-versus-interruption scene carries the personality, then gets out of the way. Schedule rows stay exceptionally simple and the cobalt current block remains unmistakable. Best balance of doodle-first identity and premium daily usability. Risk: the scene uses vertical room, so dense days need a graceful collapsed state after first scroll.

options.label: Doodle Thread
options.lineage: a hand-drawn day path running through clean native rows
options.body: The doodle becomes functional: one imperfect line connects the day, a cobalt knot marks now, and a coral loop records an interruption. It keeps more schedule visible than the scene. Risk: the hand-drawn rail must be rendered with exceptional restraint or it will feel casual instead of premium.

options.label: Doodle Companion
options.lineage: small original chosen-time vignette beside the active plan
options.body: A restrained doodle companion keeps the art present without dominating the schedule. Handwritten annotations appear only where they add human meaning. Risk: it may under-deliver on doodle-first and drift back toward the generic clean app the previous round rejected.
